hypothesis: A fixed 20% gold sleeve in a QQQ-heavy portfolio reduces realized tail risk more reliably than replacing the same 20% with SPY, without sacrificing more than 3 percentage points of annualized return.

required: Lower maximum drawdown than QQQ and QQQ80_SPY20 in both subperiods
Lower 95% monthly Expected Shortfall than both in both subperiods
Lower annualized volatility than both in both subperiods
CAGR no more than 3 percentage points below QQQ in either subperiod
adoption_rule.condition_reason: Actual cash distributions are now included, but monthly bars cannot verify intra-month maximum drawdown or daily Expected Shortfall. Canonical daily evidence is still required for USE.

data_contract.return_type: Monthly close-to-close plus actual Alpaca cash distributions with ex-date in the month; distributions are credited to the sleeve and reinvested at the monthly rebalance.

QQQ.dedup: Exact duplicate by symbol+ex_date+rate removed; QQQ 2022-09-19 rate 0.51856 appeared twice.

data_contract.missing_data_policy: No synthetic values, interpolation, estimated dividends, or alternate-feed fallback.
limitations: Monthly closes understate intra-month drawdowns and cannot produce daily Expected Shortfall.
Distribution accrual is assigned to the ex-date month; exact payable-date cash availability is not modeled.

decision.use: Keep a 20% gold sleeve as a CONDITION-level tail-risk reducer for a QQQ-heavy allocation; the conclusion survives inclusion of actual QQQ/SPY distributions.
do_not_use: Do not use gold as an expected-return timing signal.
Do not promote 20% to a production target until canonical daily data reproduces drawdown and Expected-Shortfall improvement.

prior_price_only_reference.finding: Including actual distributions increases equity returns but does not reverse the tail-risk result.
